Staff register new members and employers and update member data (names, nominees, bank details) from paper forms.
Staff investigate and merge duplicate member accounts and correct misallocated contributions with historical backdated adjustments.
Finance staff run benefit payment batches, reconcile bank payment files, and handle returned or failed payments.
Staff run annual interest or dividend crediting, produce member statements, and handle complaints about errors.
Compliance staff conduct employer inspections or audits on site, reviewing payroll records for under-declared wages.
Staff process special withdrawals such as housing, medical, or education, judging eligibility from supporting documents.
Staff prepare regulatory, actuarial, and board reports by extracting data and assembling it in spreadsheets.
Staff handle legal cases, recovery actions against defaulting employers, and appeals from members.
Vessel planners build stowage and discharge/load plans from BAPLIE files and coordinate changes with shipping lines.
Yard planners allocate stacking positions and manage yard congestion, deciding moves and housekeeping shifts.
Equipment operators (quay crane, straddle, RTG, reach stacker) execute container moves from work orders on vehicle terminals.
Gate clerks process trucks at the gate by checking documents, seals, and container damage and keying or confirming transactions in the TOS.
Control room staff dispatch equipment and resolve exceptions such as wrong container location, missing box, or equipment breakdown by radio.
Checkers and tally clerks physically verify container numbers, seals, and damage on the quay and yard and correct mismatched records.
Documentation staff process booking, release, and customs hold information from EDI and email and fix rejected EDI messages.
Berth planners schedule vessel windows and negotiate berth allocation with lines and agents when vessels arrive off schedule.
Staff manage reefer plug-ins, temperature monitoring, and dangerous goods and out-of-gauge handling compliance.
Billing staff compile storage, handling, and ancillary charges, invoice lines and consignees, and handle tariff disputes.
Staff coordinate inspections with customs and other agencies, moving boxes to inspection areas and recording outcomes.
Staff produce productivity reports (moves per hour, dwell time) and reconcile vessel move counts with lines after departure.
AP clerks receive vendor invoices by mail, email, or PDF and manually key header and line data into the AP system.
AP staff perform two- and three-way matching of invoices to POs and goods receipts and resolve price and quantity variances.
Staff chase approvers internally for invoice and requisition approvals and route exceptions by email.
AP staff answer vendor calls and emails about payment status and remittance and resolve disputes.
Buyers convert requisitions into purchase orders, select suppliers, and get quotes for spot buys.
Procurement staff negotiate prices, terms, and contracts with suppliers and run RFQ and RFP events.
Staff onboard and maintain vendor master data, including bank detail verification calls and tax forms, to prevent fraud.
AP staff prepare payment runs, select invoices for early-pay discounts or holds, and release payment files to the bank.
Receiving staff physically receive and inspect goods, then record goods receipts or report shortages and damage.
Staff reconcile vendor statements against the AP ledger and investigate duplicate payments and missing credits.
Staff perform month-end accruals for received-not-invoiced items and AP aging reconciliation to the GL.
Staff expedite late orders by calling suppliers and manage supplier performance and quality issues.
Cashier rings up customer purchases at the register: scans items, applies coupons and loyalty discounts, takes cash or card, and produces a receipt and a posted sales transaction.
Associate stocks shelves from the backroom and delivery cages, rotates product, and resets fixtures to printed planograms, physically filling gaps flagged on the replenishment list.
Service desk clerk handles returns, exchanges and price disputes, checking receipts or looking up the original sale, and keys refunds or manager override codes into the POS.
Floor associate helps customers find products, checks on-hand and other-store stock on the lookup screen, and places special or ship-to-home orders.
Receiver unloads vendor and DC deliveries, checks cartons against the PO or ASN, and posts receipts, shortages and damage claims in the system.
Associate prints shelf labels and promo signs from the weekly price-change batch, hangs them, and audits shelf price against the POS scan price.
Inventory team runs cycle counts and the annual physical count with handheld scanners, investigates variances and shrink, and posts inventory adjustments.
Merchandise planner exports sell-through and stock reports to Excel, decides markdowns and promotions, and keys the resulting price events back into the system.
Head cashier counts tills at shift close, reconciles them to the POS Z-report, logs over/short, and prepares the bank deposit and safe log.
Store manager reviews the system's suggested replenishment order and adjusts quantities by judgment for local events, weather and display needs before transmitting it.
Buyer or item-setup clerk creates new SKUs in the item master from vendor spreadsheets: cost, retail, UPC, hierarchy, tax code and supplier link.
Buyer negotiates cost, allowances and terms with vendors, then reconciles vendor deal claims, chargebacks and deductions against the promotion records.
Registrar staff answer counter, phone and email questions from students and parents about records, holds, schedules and deadlines, looking each answer up across several SIS screens.
Registration staff process add/drop and override forms, enrolling students into sections and keying prerequisite, capacity and time-conflict overrides.
Admissions or enrollment clerk keys application, transcript and residency data from forms and PDFs into a new student record and verifies the supporting documents.
Scheduler builds the master schedule or timetable, assigning sections to rooms, times and instructors and resolving conflicts by hand, often in a spreadsheet first.
Teachers or attendance clerks record daily attendance, call parents about absences, and enter excuse codes and truancy follow-ups.
Faculty enter term grades and registrar staff run grade posting, process grade-change and incomplete forms, and recalculate GPA and academic standing.
Advisors and evaluators enter transfer credit equivalencies and run degree audits, manually patching exceptions, then meet with students to plan courses and clear them for graduation.
Records staff produce official transcripts and enrollment or degree verifications for students, employers and other schools, including stamping, signing and mailing the paper copies.
Institutional research or district staff extract enrollment, demographic and completion data, clean and reconcile it in Excel, and submit state and federal compliance reports (IPEDS, state counts).
Records clerk processes FERPA releases, name and address changes, and placing or lifting registration holds, filing the signed paperwork.
Student accounts staff reconcile tuition charges, fee assessments and financial aid disbursements between the SIS and the finance system, and place or lift financial holds.
Special education or disability services staff maintain IEP or 504 accommodation records, run eligibility meetings, and push accommodation notices to instructors.
Care agent handles inbound calls and chats about bills, plan changes, outages and cancellations, toggling across CRM, billing and network screens and offering retention deals.
Sales or order-entry agent keys new activations, upgrades, moves and number ports: checks serviceability, assigns numbers and SIMs, and submits orders to provisioning.
Order-fallout team investigates orders stuck between CRM, provisioning and billing, then manually re-keys or pushes them through and contacts the customer about the delay.
Billing specialist investigates disputed charges against usage and rating records, then issues credits or adjustments within approval limits.
Collections agent works the delinquency queue, calls customers, sets payment arrangements, and triggers suspend or restore of service.
Retail store rep sells devices and plans in person, processes trade-ins and financing, activates phones, and counts handset inventory.
Dispatcher schedules field technicians for installs and repairs, and the technician completes the physical install and closes the work order with equipment serials.
Billing operations analyst runs bill-cycle QA, reviewing sample bills and rating exceptions and holding or correcting accounts before bills release.
Product or catalog analyst configures new price plans, bundles and promotions across the catalog, rating and CRM systems and tests them before launch.
Mediation or revenue-assurance analyst reprocesses rejected usage records (CDRs) and reconciles interconnect and roaming settlement files against partner invoices.
Porting desk coordinates number port-ins and port-outs with other carriers, resolving rejects caused by account or PIN mismatches.
Regulatory and tax staff prepare telecom tax, USF and complaint reports from billing extracts and respond to regulator inquiries.
Document checker examines presented LC documents (bills of lading, invoices, insurance, certificates of origin) against LC terms and UCP 600 and records any discrepancies in the system.
Compliance officer screens LC parties, vessels, ports and goods for sanctions, dual-use and trade-based money laundering red flags and investigates hits.
Operations officer keys import LC applications from client forms or portal PDFs into the trade system, checks wording, and releases the MT700 SWIFT message.
Operations staff authenticate incoming SWIFT LCs, advise or add confirmation to export LCs, and notify the beneficiary with the advice package.
Officer notifies clients of discrepancies and negotiates waivers or rejections with applicants and correspondent banks by phone, email and SWIFT MT734/MT799.
Guarantees team drafts and issues bank guarantees and standby LCs, negotiates non-standard wording with legal and the client, and handles claims.
Settlement staff process reimbursement claims and payments (MT103/MT202), book FX and fees, and reconcile nostro accounts.
Relationship manager advises corporate clients on structuring and pricing trade deals and gathers KYC and onboarding documents.
Officer processes LC amendments (MT707), tracks beneficiary acceptance, and updates the outstanding liability.
Credit or operations staff check and book each transaction against the client's trade facility limits, cash margin or collateral, and get approval for any excess.
Collections officer handles documentary collections, releasing documents against payment or acceptance and chasing unpaid drawees.
Back-office clerk logs, scans, couriers and archives original paper trade documents and keeps the physical document vault in order.
Meter reader walks or drives routes to read meters on a handheld, uploads reads, and billing staff review high, low and estimated read exceptions.
Billing analyst works the bill-exception queue, correcting reads, rate codes or account setup on held bills before releasing them.
Call-center rep handles customer calls about high bills, payment arrangements, outages and account questions, explaining usage history from CIS screens.
Customer service staff key start, stop and transfer-of-service orders for move-ins and move-outs, including deposits and final bills.
Dispatcher issues field service orders for connects, disconnects, meter exchanges and investigations, and technicians do the physical work and close the orders.
Collections staff send shutoff notices, apply regulatory protections such as medical certificates and winter moratoria, then schedule disconnections and reconnections.
Payment processing clerk posts lockbox, agent and online payments, fixes misapplied payments, and reconciles daily cash to the general ledger.
Large-account or commercial billing specialist hand-calculates and checks complex bills (demand, time-of-use, net metering, multi-meter) and corrects the CIS output.
Rate analyst configures tariff changes from a rate case decision in the CIS and runs parallel test bills to confirm the new calculations.
Meter asset staff track meter inventory, testing and AMI communication failures, and resync records between the meter data system and the CIS.
Assistance-program staff enroll low-income customers, post agency pledges and grants, and apply discount rates to accounts.
Regulatory staff respond to utility commission complaints and compile billing, disconnection and arrears reports for regulators.
Picker walks or drives to locations from RF-gun prompts or paper pick lists, picks units or cases, and confirms each pick by scan.
Packer and shipper pack orders, weigh and label cartons, manifest with the carrier, and load outbound trailers.
Receiver unloads inbound trailers, checks quantities and condition against the ASN or PO, labels pallets with license plates, and keys receipts and damage.
Forklift operator moves received pallets to putaway locations and runs replenishment moves from reserve to pick faces as the system directs.
Inventory control clerk runs cycle counts, investigates location and quantity variances, and posts adjustments in the WMS.
Shift supervisor plans and releases pick waves, assigns workers to zones by judgment of volume and cutoff times, and rebalances labor during the shift.
Inventory or systems staff resolve exceptions such as short picks, wrong locations and WMS-to-ERP interface failures, re-keying orders or inventory transactions by hand.
Dock scheduler books carrier appointments, manages yard and door assignments, and handles late or unscheduled trucks by phone.
Returns processor inspects returned goods, grades their condition, and restocks, refurbishes or disposes of them while recording the disposition.
Value-added services crew kits, assembles, relabels or bundles products to work orders.
Inventory analyst maintains item dimensions and location master data and runs slotting analysis in Excel to move fast movers closer to shipping.
Supervisor or trainer runs safety checks on equipment and trains new and temp workers on RF screens and pick procedures.
Operations analyst reconciles daily positions, transactions and cash in the portfolio accounting system against custodian feeds and researches and clears breaks.
Reporting team produces quarterly client performance reports, checks returns and holdings for errors, and assembles and distributes the report packages.
Advisor meets clients to review performance and financial plans, learn about goals and life changes, and explain fees and allocations.
Operations staff process corporate actions (dividends, splits, mergers, voluntary elections) and fix the cost basis and holdings they affect.
Pricing analyst validates vendor security prices and manually prices illiquid, private and hard-to-value holdings.
Alternatives analyst keys capital calls, distributions and NAV statements from private fund PDFs into the accounting system.
Onboarding specialist collects account paperwork and custodial forms, initiates ACATS and other asset transfers, and sets up the account and its fee schedule in the system.
Service associate processes withdrawals, wires and journals, doing verbal callback verification and getting approval for each one.
Portfolio manager or advisor reviews model drift and cash needs, decides on rebalancing, and generates and submits trades.
Billing analyst calculates AUM-based advisory fees, handles household groupings and fee exceptions, and produces invoices or custodian fee debit files.
Tax staff reconcile cost basis and realized gains to custodian 1099s and support tax-loss harvesting and accountant requests.
Compliance officer reviews trades, client communications and books and records for regulatory exams and Form ADV updates.
